introduction: Today we celebrate the Baptism of the Lord, which ends the Christmas season. Isaiah describes the servant of the Lord, on whom God has put his Spirit, who will not break a bruised reed. Peter tells how God anointed Jesus with the Holy Spirit and power. In the Gospel, Jesus is baptized by John, the heavens open, and the Father says, This is my beloved Son. Let us give thanks for our own Baptism.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, in Baptism we became children of God. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that all the baptized may live as beloved children of God and servants of his justice. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those preparing for Baptism, and for their families: that they may receive this gift with faith and joy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the bruised and the weak: that they may be treated with the gentleness of the Lord's servant. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have forgotten their Baptism: that they may rediscover the love of the Father. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that, like Jesus, we may go about doing good. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty God, at the Jordan you declared Jesus your beloved Son. Keep us, your children by water and the Spirit, faithful to our Baptism all our lives. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: My beloved Son
reflection.body:
Isaiah describes a mysterious servant chosen by God: "Behold, my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights: I have put my Spirit on him." This servant will bring justice to the nations, but in a gentle way: "He won't break a bruised reed. He won't quench a dimly burning wick." He will be "a light for the nations, to open the blind eyes."

In the Gospel, Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John. John protests: "I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?" John's baptism was for sinners, and Jesus has no sin. But Jesus insists: "Allow it now, for this is the fitting way for us to fulfill all righteousness." Jesus steps into the water alongside sinners. From the very beginning of his mission, he stands with us.

As he comes up from the water, "the heavens were opened to him," and he sees the Spirit of God coming down like a dove. Then a voice from heaven says, "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased." These words echo Isaiah's servant "in whom my soul delights." Jesus is both the beloved Son and the gentle servant.

In the second reading, Peter sums up the ministry that began that day: "God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil."

In our Baptism, the Father said to each of us: you are my beloved child. And we received the Spirit to continue Christ's mission of doing good.

This week, find out the date of your Baptism and give thanks for it. When you bless yourself with holy water, remember that you are God's beloved. And look for one way to go about doing good, gently, like the servant of the Lord.
